Answer Part 1 (Cont.): Peer Review Dialogues with Blocking Quality Gate

Quality Gate Enforced: Round 1 of PR #38 peer review identified 4 critical architectural gaps (missing ActionStatus lifecycle, in-memory concurrency vs integer OCC, incomplete resolution gate, and missing append-only status history). Author remediation was completed and verified before any implementation was allowed into lab4-staging.

Peer Review Dialogue Snippet on PR #38 (Issue #37)

Participant Dialogue & Technical Verification
Reviewer (@pimchayasupr-hash) "Blocking Concerns (P1): (1) ActionTaken requires ActionStatus enum and assignee relation. Result mandatory only upon COMPLETED. Reject inactive assignees with 400. (2) Non-atomic timestamp comparisons are unsafe; use integer version with atomic write predicates (409 Conflict). (3) Resolution Gate must verify 4 prerequisites. (4) TicketStatusHistory must atomically append in same prisma transaction."
Author (@supa-gif173) "Updated all four specification documents in commit 1064b9d: Added ActionStatus, assigneeId relation, 400 INACTIVE_ASSIGNEE, terminal action lock, integer version field with compare-and-increment OCC write predicates, 4-condition resolution gate, TicketStatusHistory model, and aligned Zen Green tokens. All regression suites 100% green."
Reviewer (@pimchayasupr-hash) "Verified updates in commit 1064b9d. Full compliance with Course Engineering Specifications. LGTM and Approved! Proceed with merge into lab4-staging."

Answer Part 2: Spec DD (Engineering Specifications)

The approved engineering contract is documented in docs/lab-04/specification.md. Below are the key architectural requirements and business rules.

Key Functional Requirements & Business Rules

Rule ID Scope Engineering Specification & Contract Details
FR-01 / BR-03 Actions Taken Lifecycle ActionTaken records actionDateTime, assigneeId, status (PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, CANCELLED), description, result, followUpRequired, followUpNote, attachmentNotes. Result mandatory only upon COMPLETED. Terminal lock on COMPLETED/CANCELLED.
FR-02 / BR-04 RBAC & Requester Isolation Requesters have read-only visibility for owned tickets. Creating/updating actions returns 403 Forbidden. Client-supplied requesterId cannot override JWT.
BR-02 Assignee Validation Assignee must be an active user with role STAFF or ADMIN. Attempt to assign to inactive user returns HTTP 400 with code INACTIVE_ASSIGNEE.
FR-05 / BR-06 Resolution Gate Transition to RESOLVED blocked with HTTP 400 unless: (1) Ticket owner assigned, (2) >=1 ActionTaken exists, (3) >=1 action is COMPLETED with non-empty result, and (4) all follow-up notes are documented.
FR-06 / BR-07 Advisory Resolution Requester toggle sets problemAppearsResolved = true without mutating authoritative ticket status.
FR-09 / BR-11 Optimistic Concurrency (OCC) Integer version on Ticket and ActionTaken. Mutations execute updateMany({ where: { id, version: expectedVersion } }) inside prisma.$transaction returning HTTP 409 Conflict on collision.
FR-11 / BR-13 Append-Only Status History Status transitions atomically append an audit row to TicketStatusHistory (fromStatus, toStatus, changedById, changedAt). No update/delete routes exist.

My Reflection on AI Specification-Agent and Coding-Agent Use

  
Specification-Agent Use: Working with the AI specification agent before implementation was crucial for eliminating ambiguity. Decomposing stakeholder expectations into numbered, measurable requirements (FRs, BRs, ACs) prevented scope creep. When our peer reviewer identified the need for optimistic concurrency via integer versioning and append-only audit logs, the specification agent enabled us to systematically update all contract files and planned test cases before touching production code.

  
Coding-Agent Use: The AI coding agent accelerated delivery of complex full-stack features while maintaining production rigor. It excelled at enforcing atomic Prisma transactions, generating idempotent test fixtures, ensuring explicit SVG dimensions (<= 64px), and building comprehensive Vitest and Playwright test suites. Overall, Sprint 4 proved that pairing human architectural oversight with disciplined AI coding agents produces robust, test-verified software.

Inactive Assignee Validation & Terminal Action Lock Logic

  
// server/src/routes/actions.ts: Assignee & Terminal State Guardrails
if (assigneeId) {
  const assignee = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: assigneeId } });
  if (!assignee || !assignee.isActive || !['STAFF', 'ADMIN'].includes(assignee.role)) {
    return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Assignee must be an active IT Staff or Administrator.', code: 'INACTIVE_ASSIGNEE' });
  }
}
if (['COMPLETED', 'CANCELLED'].includes(existingAction.status)) {
  return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Terminal actions cannot be modified.', code: 'TERMINAL_ACTION_LOCKED' });
}
